skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

70. as they are now"). It also would not unblock the postconditions (Approach 2/3).

78.    --> src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs:534:44      (pd.read(pde_idx))
79.    ::: src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs:205:13

81. 
82. error: precondition not satisfied
83.    --> src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs:549:9       (PAGE_TABLE_ALLOCATOR.alloc_as::<…>())
84.    ::: src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs:350:18
85. 350 |   requires bump_view(self).inv(),                    <- failed precondition

94.    ::: src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs:205:13
95. 205 |             index@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,   <- failed precondition

97. error: postcondition not satisfied                        (×3 exits)
98.    --> src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs:706:13
99. 706 |  Ok(_) => identity_map_view().accessible(phys_addr@),
100. ```
101. 
102. - **`bump_view(self).inv()` (line 549).** `bump_view` is
103.   `pub uninterp spec fn bump_view(...) -> BumpView` over the module-level `static
104.   PAGE_TABLE_ALLOCATOR`. `inv()` is a non-trivial conjunction of facts about that
105.   opaque value; nothing in `bump_allocator` (no lemma/axiom — `new()` has an empty
106.   `ensures`) establishes `inv()` for the static. By design its realization is
107.   "deferred to the proving phase" (lib.spec.rs:166-169). I cannot establish `inv()`
108.   of an uninterpreted value, and I am forbidden from adding an axiom/`assume_spec`.
109. - **`mapped.contains(...)` (618) / `accessible(...)` (706).** See Approach 3 — these
110.   are logically unprovable while `identity_map_view()` is a parameterless constant.
111. 
112. #### Approach 3 — make `identity_map_view()` concrete (to try to prove the postconditions)
113. 
114. Set `identity_map_view() = { initialized: false, mapped: Set::empty() }`, removed
115. admits, re-ran. Still **6 verified, 3 errors**:
116. 
117. ```
118. error: postcondition not satisfied
119.    --> src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs:618:13
120. 618 | Ok(_) => identity_map_view().mapped.contains(spec_page_base(phys_addr as int)),
121.         ... at exit 639 | return Ok(());
122.         # Set::empty().contains(p) == false  →  Ok-branch is unprovable
123. 
124. error: postcondition not satisfied
125.    --> src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs:706:13
126. 706 | Ok(_) => identity_map_view().accessible(phys_addr@),
127.         ... at the Err exits (730 `ensure_pt(...)?`, end of body)
128.         # accessible = (!initialized || …) = (!false) = true  →  Err => !accessible
129.         #   becomes Err => false, unprovable
130. ```
131. 
132. This is the decisive demonstration the reviewer asked for: a **concrete** view cannot
133. satisfy the contract either. The two functions each assert a **result-dependent pair**
134. over the *same* fixed view —
135. `ensure_pte`: `Ok => mapped.contains(p)` **and** `Err => !mapped.contains(p)`;
136. `identity_map_page`: `Ok => accessible(p)` **and** `Err => !accessible(p)`.

138. fixed truth value, so exactly one of the two clauses becomes `=> false`. The exec
139. return decision (PTE read result, frame-number range, `pd_paddr == 0`) is not tied to
140. that fixed set. **No proof, lemma (`lemma_install_page_maps`, `lemma_map_page_*`), or
141. `vstd` search can discharge both clauses** — it is a logical impossibility, not a
142. proof-engineering gap. (The proof.rs lemmas prove facts about `spec_install_page` /
143. `spec_map_page` *transitions* `v -> v'`, but the contracts are written over a single
144. `v` with no `old`/`new` distinction, so the lemmas have nothing to connect to.)
145.

147.

149. real page-table memory, and `ensure_pte`'s `pt.write(pte_idx, present_pte)` must be
150. shown to make that PTE present. But `Table::write`
151. (`src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs:246`) has **no contents `ensures`** —
152. deliberately: `tcb-allowed.md` records that pinning the pure global ghost
153. `spec_table_word(addr,index)` to the written `entry` on an `external_body` (assumed)
154. write is **unsound** (two writes of distinct entries to one slot would assume
155. `e1 == e2`, i.e. `false`). The genuine `old@ -> @` slot transition is therefore
156. deferred to the proving-phase page-table permission token. `table.rs` is **not in
157. scope** for this task, and I am forbidden from (a) changing exec signatures of the
158. out-of-scope callers (`init`/`ensure_identity_mapped_range` at line 134, `memset`,
159. `memcpy`) to thread a `Tracked` token, (b) adding an `external_body` not in
160. `tcb-allowed.md`, or (c) adding an `assume_specification`/`axiom`.
161. 
162. #### Specific guidance requested
163. 
164. The three target functions cannot reach `admit=0` without one of the following,
165. each currently out of this module's scope:
166. 
167. 1. **A spec-readable model of the singleton state** — replace the `uninterp`
168.    `identity_map_view()` / `bump_view()` with a ghost token (`PointsTo` /
169.    atomic-ghost / global invariant) over `KERNEL_PD_PADDR` and `PAGE_TABLE_ALLOCATOR`.
170.    Requires exec changes to module statics and out-of-scope callers.
171. 2. **A sound `old@ -> @` contents postcondition on `arch::…::Table::write`** (and the
172.    matching permission token), which `tcb-allowed.md` documents as deliberately
173.    deferred-because-unsound-for-`external_body`. `table.rs` is out of scope.
174. 3. **Approval to add a precondition** `requires pde_idx@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` /
175.    `pte_idx@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` to `ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte` (to fix the line-534/631
176.    read preconditions only — does not touch the 549/618/706 blockers).
177.

 `Table::read` requires `index@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`. `TableIndex` carries that as a
 type invariant in the **arch** crate, but it is not usable cross-crate:
 
 ```
 error: Verus Internal Error: missing type invariant function
    --> src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs:534:33
 ```
 
 So the index bound cannot be recovered inside `ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte`. The only sound
 way to get it is to **add `requires pde_idx@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH`** to `ensure_pt`'s
 contract (and the `pte_idx` analogue to `ensure_pte`) — a **contract/signature
 change** the Turn-1 constraint explicitly forbids ("contracts must remain as strong
 as they are now"). It also would not unblock the postconditions (Approach 2/3).

 #### Approach 3 — make `identity_map_view()` concrete (to try to prove the postconditions)
 
 Set `identity_map_view() = { initialized: false, mapped: Set::empty() }`, removed
 admits, re-ran. Still **6 verified, 3 errors**:
 
 ```
 error: postcondition not satisfied
    --> src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs:618:13
 618 | Ok(_) => identity_map_view().mapped.contains(spec_page_base(phys_addr as int)),
         ... at exit 639 | return Ok(());
         # Set::empty().contains(p) == false  →  Ok-branch is unprovable
 
 error: postcondition not satisfied
    --> src/kernel/src/mm/virt/identity_map.rs:706:13
 706 | Ok(_) => identity_map_view().accessible(phys_addr@),
         ... at the Err exits (730 `ensure_pt(...)?`, end of body)
         # accessible = (!initialized || …) = (!false) = true  →  Err => !accessible
         #   becomes Err => false, unprovable
 ```
 
 This is the decisive demonstration the reviewer asked for: a **concrete** view cannot
 satisfy the contract either. The two functions each assert a **result-dependent pair**
 over the *same* fixed view —
 `ensure_pte`: `Ok => mapped.contains(p)` **and** `Err => !mapped.contains(p)`;
 `identity_map_page`: `Ok => accessible(p)` **and** `Err => !accessible(p)`.
 For any fixed value of `identity_map_view()`, `contains(p)`/`accessible(p)` has one
 fixed truth value, so exactly one of the two clauses becomes `=> false`. The exec
 return decision (PTE read result, frame-number range, `pd_paddr == 0`) is not tied to
 that fixed set. **No proof, lemma (`lemma_install_page_maps`, `lemma_map_page_*`), or
 `vstd` search can discharge both clauses** — it is a logical impossibility, not a
 proof-engineering gap. (The proof.rs lemmas prove facts about `spec_install_page` /
 `spec_map_page` *transitions* `v -> v'`, but the contracts are written over a single
 `v` with no `old`/`new` distinction, so the lemmas have nothing to connect to.)
 
 #### Why a sound full fix is out of scope
 
 To make the postconditions provable, `identity_map_view().mapped` must reflect the
 real page-table memory, and `ensure_pte`'s `pt.write(pte_idx, present_pte)` must be
 shown to make that PTE present. But `Table::write`
 (`src/libs/arch/src/x86/mem/paging/table.rs:246`) has **no contents `ensures`** —
 deliberately: `tcb-allowed.md` records that pinning the pure global ghost
 `spec_table_word(addr,index)` to the written `entry` on an `external_body` (assumed)
 write is **unsound** (two writes of distinct entries to one slot would assume
 `e1 == e2`, i.e. `false`). The genuine `old@ -> @` slot transition is therefore
 deferred to the proving-phase page-table permission token. `table.rs` is **not in
 scope** for this task, and I am forbidden from (a) changing exec signatures of the
 out-of-scope callers (`init`/`ensure_identity_mapped_range` at line 134, `memset`,
 `memcpy`) to thread a `Tracked` token, (b) adding an `external_body` not in
 `tcb-allowed.md`, or (c) adding an `assume_specification`/`axiom`.
 
 #### Specific guidance requested
 
 The three target functions cannot reach `admit=0` without one of the following,
 each currently out of this module's scope:
 
 1. **A spec-readable model of the singleton state** — replace the `uninterp`
    `identity_map_view()` / `bump_view()` with a ghost token (`PointsTo` /
    atomic-ghost / global invariant) over `KERNEL_PD_PADDR` and `PAGE_TABLE_ALLOCATOR`.
    Requires exec changes to module statics and out-of-scope callers.
 2. **A sound `old@ -> @` contents postcondition on `arch::…::Table::write`** (and the
    matching permission token), which `tcb-allowed.md` documents as deliberately
    deferred-because-unsound-for-`external_body`. `table.rs` is out of scope.
 3. **Approval to add a precondition** `requires pde_idx@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` /
    `pte_idx@ < PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH` to `ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte` (to fix the line-534/631
    read preconditions only — does not touch the 549/618/706 blockers).
 
 Items (1) and (2) are the shared "proving-phase ghost-token" framework every sibling
 `mm::phys::*` singleton free function defers; building it is a cross-module change
 beyond `mm::virt::identity_map`. Detailed reproduction recorded in
 `verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-virt-identity-map/verification_todo.md`.
